newsitem.title: USA: Minerals Technologies sets German operation.
newsitem.headline: Minerals Technologies sets German operation.

text.p: Minerals Technologies Inc said Friday it will build and operate a satellite precipitated calcium carbonate (PCC) plant at Haindl Papier GmbH's paper mill in Schongau, Germany.
The satellite plant will produce PCC for filling improved newsprint paper produced at the Schongau mill and for filling supercalendered and film-coated offset paper at Haindl's Augsburg mill.

The satellite plant will, in cooperation with Haindl Papier, be used to further develop Minerals Technologies' patented recycled mineral filler, Envirofil PCC, for use in the paper production process, the company said.

The plant will be equal to about two satellite units and is scheduled to begin operation for PCC production in the first quarter of 1998. A satellite unit produces between 25,000 and 35,000 tons of PCC annually. This one will be the company's 51st worldwide and first in Germany.
